# The Slow Crisis of the Millbrook Bridge

Imagine a bridge. Call it the Millbrook Bridge: a two-lane steel girder crossing over the Millbrook River, built in 1958 to carry farm trucks and a few thousand cars a day between the towns of Millbrook and Harrow. It is 60 metres long, painted green, and mostly ignored by the people who drive over it. Until, one spring, the engineers start asking uncomfortable questions.

## What the inspections actually find

Bridges in most countries are inspected on a regular schedule — typically every one or two years, with deeper dives every five or six. Inspectors walk the deck, crawl under the girders, and look for the unglamorous evidence of decay: rust
